title: Console: add usage analytics filter for template-tagged traffic
author: Logan Wright
release_notes: - Console usage analytics: add a filter to view only traffic tagged as quickstart-template generated (opt-in). - Adds backend query support and guards to avoid high-cardinality dimensions.
body:
Title: Console: add usage analytics filter for template-tagged traffic

Context
DevEx quickstart templates optionally tag API traffic so we can measure adoption/activation without relying on inference logs or user self-reporting (PM-912). PR-18421 added a whitelist + validation for the template telemetry headers at the gateway. This PR completes the loop on the Console side by adding a first-class filter in Usage Analytics dashboards to view only “template-generated” traffic.

Goals
- Add a low-cardinality, privacy-safe way to filter usage analytics to template-tagged traffic.
- Keep existing dashboards/backfills working for customers that do not send the template tag.
- Avoid introducing any tag values or user-provided strings into analytics dimensions.

Non-goals
- Building a new dashboard; this is a filter + query update on existing Usage Analytics views.
- Capturing template version, template name, repo, CLI version, etc. (explicitly avoided due to cardinality + privacy; if we need this later we’ll do a separate proposal with sampling and explicit consent).

What changed (high level)
Backend
- Introduced a derived boolean dimension `is_template_traffic` into the usage rollup query layer.
- Added a query param and API contract update to `GET /console/api/usage/rollups` (and the equivalent GraphQL resolver) to allow filtering by `is_template_traffic=true|false`.
- Filtering is done at query time against the aggregated table when available; if the dimension is missing (older partitions / partial backfill), the API returns `400` only if the client explicitly requests the filter and the selected range includes unsupported partitions. Console handles this by showing an inline notice and automatically narrowing to supported ranges (see UI notes).

Console UI
- Added a filter chip in Usage Analytics: “Traffic origin: Template (quickstarts)”. When enabled it adds `is_template_traffic=true` to the query.
- Added a tooltip clarifying that this requires opt-in template tagging and may not include all historical traffic.
- Added an “info” callout when the filter is active but the selected time range contains unsupported partitions.

Data semantics / privacy
- The filter is based on presence of the validated template-origin marker only. We do not store the raw header value, and the pipeline coerces it to a boolean.
- No per-request IDs, template names, or user-provided strings are emitted into analytics dimensions.
- `is_template_traffic` is not joinable to PII and does not increase tag cardinality.

API contract
- REST: `GET /console/api/usage/rollups?start=...&end=...&is_template_traffic=true`
- GraphQL: `usageRollups(filter: { isTemplateTraffic: true })`
- Default remains unchanged (no filter applied).

Implementation details
- Rollup query builder: added a guarded WHERE clause to restrict to `is_template_traffic = true` when requested.
- Added a small compatibility shim so internal callers that pass an unrecognized filter get a structured error with a remediation link.
- Added unit tests for the query builder and resolver validation.
- Added snapshot tests for the Console filter chip and URL state.

Error handling
- If the user enables the filter and selects a range that spans unsupported partitions, the API responds with `422` and includes `first_supported_timestamp` in the error detail. Console catches this and offers “Adjust range” (one-click) rather than failing the entire view.

Why not dimension on template name/version?
Discussed with Observability (Allison/Caleb) and PM (Nikhil): high-cardinality risk and potential privacy concerns. The purpose of v1 is adoption measurement + funnel analysis at an aggregate level; template name/version can be evaluated later via explicit eventing rather than piggybacking on inference requests.

Testing
- Unit: added coverage for query builder filter behavior and validation.
- Integration: exercised staging Console with seeded template-tagged traffic; verified filter toggling updates all widgets consistently.
- UI: snapshot tests for filter chip state + empty-state messaging.

Rollout plan
- This is safe to deploy dark: filter exists but only returns non-empty results if traffic is tagged.
- No migration required; the derived dimension is already present for new partitions. For older partitions it’s best-effort.

Screenshots
- Included in the PR attachments: Usage Analytics page with “Traffic origin: Template (quickstarts)” enabled, showing reduced traffic and a note about opt-in tagging.

Linked work
- Gateway header allowlist: PR-18421
- Template adoption telemetry requirements: PM-912
- Observability pack integration (dashboards/filters alignment): ENG-4184

Checklist
- [x] Low-cardinality dimension only
- [x] No raw header values persisted
- [x] Backward compatible API
- [x] Console UX handles partial availability
- [x] Tests added

Commits
- feat(console-usage): add is_template_traffic filter to rollup query builder
- feat(console-ui): add Traffic origin filter chip and URL state
- fix(console-ui): handle 422 partial-availability errors with suggested range
- test(usage): add resolver validation + query builder unit tests
- docs(internal): update analytics filter contract notes

Changed areas/files (representative)
- console/server/routes/usage_rollups.ts
- console/server/graphql/resolvers/usageRollups.ts
- console/server/analytics/query_builder.ts
- console/web/src/pages/usage/UsageFilters.tsx
- console/web/src/pages/usage/useUsageQueryState.ts
- console/web/src/pages/usage/__tests__/UsageFilters.test.tsx
- console/server/__tests__/usage_rollups_filtering.test.ts

Example (illustrative)
- Before: /usage?range=7d
- After: /usage?range=7d&isTemplateTraffic=true

Review conversation (highlights)
Allison Grant: Please confirm we are not persisting the header payload and that this stays boolean-only. Also, ensure metric dimensions don’t grow.
Logan Wright: Confirmed. Pipeline maps to boolean at ingestion; query only sees `is_template_traffic`. Added a guard + comment in query builder and tests to prevent additional origin dimensions.

Caleb Johnson: The 400/422 behavior—can we avoid breaking existing clients?
Logan Wright: Existing clients never pass the filter, so default behavior unchanged. For filter users, changed to 422 with remediation payload; UI handles and offers range adjust.

Monica Patel: Can we align naming with DevEx docs (“template-tagged traffic”)?
Logan Wright: Updated UI string to “Template (quickstarts)” and tooltip uses “template-tagged traffic (opt-in)”.

Sergio Costa: Can this be used for dashboards/alerts in the observability pack?
Logan Wright: Yes, but this PR is Console-only. I added an internal note on the filter param so pack can link to pre-filtered views; separate PR can add deep links.

Nikhil Sharma: Any privacy review needed?
Logan Wright: Kept strictly boolean. Added note in code that raw header values are dropped and not queryable. Linked SUP-29458 as motivation for opt-in + proxy compatibility.

CI
- build-console: PASS
- lint: PASS
- unit-tests: PASS
- web-tests (jest): PASS
- typecheck: PASS

Merge
Squash merged into main by Logan Wright on 2025-03-04.

Follow-ups
- Add docs-site snippet showing how to enable template tagging (DevEx) and how to use this filter for KPI tracking (PM-912).
- Consider adding a “Template traffic” saved view link from quickstarts docs once public launch is ready.
